system.aoe: One creature, one item, or area (see below)
system.description:
Ceremony has several uses in a religious organization, depending on the cleric’s level. It leaves no aura of magic, though in some cases an aura of good or evil might remain (and so be detectable). The exact ceremonies vary from religion to religion, but usually include these:

  • 1st-level cleric: coming of age, burial, marriage
  • 3rd-level cleric: dedication, investiture, consecrate item
  • 5th-level cleric: ordination, special vows
  • 7th-level cleric: consecrate ground
  • 9th-level cleric: anathematize

Each needs a cleric of at least the listed level, with further limits given below. Except for anathematize, no saving throw applies, since the recipient is either an object or presumed willing; any version but anathematize simply fails if cast on a person who (for some reason) does not want it.

Coming of age: a limited bless cast on a young man (in some cultures a young woman) fairly early in life, often at age 12. The young person gets a + 1 bonus on any single saving throw, which can be used at any time after the ceremony. In some cultures an adolescent must receive this blessing before enjoying the rights and privileges of an adult.

Burial: magically protects a corpse and gives it the blessing of the religion. The body is shielded for one week as if by protection from evil, and anyone trying to dig it up within that time must save versus spell or stop and flee in fear for one turn.

Marriage: has no tangible effect (it does not guarantee happiness or harmony), but usually carries moral or legal weight, much like marriage rites in our real world.

Dedication: takes the recipient into the ranks of the cleric’s religion as a sanctioned worshiper of the cleric’s deity. It is permanent unless the worshiper shows a desire to change allegiance to another deity; then a new dedication by a cleric of higher level than the one who performed the earlier one can override it.

Investiture: must be performed on any aspiring cleric before that character can become a first-level cleric.

Consecrate item: must be performed on any object to be placed on an altar or elsewhere in a religious building. Holy (or unholy) water must be kept in a properly consecrated container or it loses its potency.

Ordination: must be performed on a cleric before he or she can become the priest of a congregation or take on similar duties; even an adventuring cleric must be ordained before gaining followers and establishing a following or other group. The ordaining cleric must be of higher level than the recipient. It is often part of the training a cleric receives to advance from second to third level.

Special vows: can be taken by a would-be cavalier or paladin before beginning that career. They last until the character has enough experience points to reach the upper limit of his or her current level, and can then be renewed during training between levels, or at any time while advancing through the next level. While the vows last, the character is immune to bestow curse spells (but not cursed items), but saves at −4 against any quest spell cast by a cleric of the same alignment as the cleric who gave the vows.

Consecrate ground: should be performed on a site before any holy (unholy) building is built there. A religious building on unconsecrated ground slowly but surely falls into disrepair, with a 1% cumulative chance per year of actually collapsing. The spell must be cast before the area is changed in any way (landscaping, for example) and before any building materials arrive; done as an afterthought, it has no effect. It can also be cast on land meant to be a graveyard: the graveyard then automatically turns undead each round as a 3rd-level cleric. If an evil cleric consecrates the graveyard, undead there are treated as protected and controlled by a 3rd-level evil cleric.

Anathematize: a form of excommunication that literally brands the offender on the cheek, forehead, arm or hand with a symbol, sigil or sign marking him or her (to those who understand it) as having committed a serious offense in the eyes of the deity. An unwilling subject saves versus spell at −4 to avoid it. If the subject does not truly deserve the brand, the spell fails. A successful atonement makes the brand fade, and possibly vanish: if the offenses were caused by magic or some other outside force, it disappears completely; if they were the subject’s own doing, it can never be completely removed.

Components and costs: components vary by religion, but always involve the cleric’s holy symbol in some way. Standard fees: coming of age, 5-15 sp; burial, 5-50 gp; marriage, 1-20 gp; dedication, 1-10 sp (or sometimes free); investiture, 1-100 gp (or sometimes free); item consecration, usually free; ordination, usually free but possibly as much as 200 gp; special vows, 1-100 gp (or sometimes free); consecrate ground, 100-600 gp depending on the size of the area and the cleric’s level; anathematize is always free, since it is always considered in the religion’s best interests.

Three to five clerics combine their power so that one of them casts a spell or turns undead more effectively. The highest-level cleric (or one of them) stands in the middle while the others join hands in a circle around him or her, and all cast combine together.

The central cleric temporarily acts as one level higher for each cleric in the circle, up to four levels, for up to 3 turns. The increase applies to the cleric’s effective level for turning undead and for spell details that depend on the caster’s level. The central cleric gains no extra spells, but can cast spells already memorized, often with improved effects.

The clerics in the circle must concentrate on keeping up the effect. They lose any armor class bonus from shield or dexterity, and attackers get +4 on all “to hit” rolls against them.

Protects the recipient from normal extremes of cold or of heat (depending on the version). He or she can stand unclothed in temperatures as low as -30° F. or as high as 130° F. with no ill effect. Beyond those limits, the recipient takes 1 hit point of exposure damage per hour for each degree past the limit. (Without such protection, exposure damage is 1 hit point per turn for each degree.)

The spell lasts its full duration unless the recipient is affected by any magical cold (including white dragon breath) or magical heat, which ends it whichever version was cast (endure cold is ended by magical heat or fire as well as by magical cold). The recipient takes no damage from that magical heat or cold in the round the spell breaks, but is vulnerable to it from the next round on. The spell also ends at once if resist fire or resist cold is cast on the recipient.

Much like sanctuary, but it affects only undead of 4 or fewer hit dice. A saving throw versus spell is made for each type of undead within 30 feet of the caster. If it fails, all undead of that type completely ignore the caster for the duration (which also means the caster cannot later turn them). If it succeeds, all undead of that type attack the caster in preference to anyone else.

The spell ends if the caster attacks or tries to cast any other spell. If the caster is neutral (with respect to good and evil), the undead save at -2. Component: the cleric’s holy symbol.

The cleric picks up a small stone or pebble and places a magical aura on it (stones already magical cannot be affected). It can be thrown at a target up to 4˝ away (with no obstacles and enough headroom). It counts as a +1 weapon “to hit” and does 1 point of damage if it hits. Ranges are 2˝/3˝/4˝, with the standard modifiers. If it goes more than 4˝ from the thrower or misses, it loses its dweomer and falls harmlessly. It must be thrown within 6 rounds of casting or it becomes ordinary again.

A hit breaks a spell caster’s concentration only if the victim fails a saving throw versus spell. Targets with innate magic resistance cannot be affected. A shield spell, a brooch of shielding, protection from normal missiles, a minor globe of invulnerability, or any similar (more powerful) magic protects against it.

Number of stones: 2 for a cleric of 6th through 10th level, 3 at 11th through 15th, plus one more for every five levels beyond the 11th (4 stones at 16th level, 5 at 21st, etc.). The cleric can give the stones to another character to throw. Some religions may forbid their clerics this spell, since it lets them use a missile weapon (of sorts).

The cleric can see through a disguise made only of makeup or altered clothing (that is, non-magical). The spell shows only that the target is posing as someone or something else, not the target’s true class or profession or real appearance. It does not detect actual rank or status, cannot reveal an illusion as such, and cannot detect any deception about alignment, but it can tell whether a figure is the subject of a friends spell.

The target gets a saving throw versus spell. If it succeeds, the disguise looks even more convincing to the cleric, who becomes sure the target really is what he claims. A bless spell, magic armor, or a magic item of protection (such as a cloak or ring) gives the target an appropriate bonus on the save.

The cleric learns something of his or her own, or another figure’s, future “luck”: a bonus or penalty that will apply to one “to hit” roll or saving throw at some point the subject does not know.

Secret rolls: the DM rolls 1d12 for when it happens and 1d6 for the effect (1 = -3; 2 = -2; 3 = -1; 4 = +1; 5 = +2; 6 = +3). From the d6, the DM tells the cleric’s player whether the portent is good, fair (moderately good or moderately bad) or poor; the subject is usually told too.

Counting: the d12 result is the number of rolls the subject must make before the one affected: on a 12, the 12th such roll afterwards gets the portent. Only rolls in life-or-death (combat or peril) situations count: saving throws in combat or against magic, the subject’s own “to hit” rolls, and opponents’ “to hit” rolls against the subject. The count stops if the character tries to “sidestep” the portent with, for instance, saving throws against harmless effects.

The affected roll is adjusted up or down by the d6 result, making the character more or less likely to hit, to be hit, or to make the saving throw.

Component: a numbered wheel or tea leaves.

All water vapor in the air in the area of effect falls as a light rain. (Low-level casters will certainly be inside the area themselves.) It lasts only 1 segment per level of the caster, and only about 1/100 of an inch falls per segment, so the general effects are:

  • Thin, light material is damp after 1 segment and soaked thereafter.
  • Twigs and heavy material such as canvas are damp after 2 segments and wet thereafter.
  • Flat, fairly non-porous surfaces (stone floors, rock, painted wood, etc.) are damp after 1 segment and filmed with water thereafter.
  • Semi-porous surfaces and materials are damp on the surface after 2 segments; the dampness then works inward until they are thoroughly wet after 5 segments.
  • Porous surfaces and materials simply soak up the rain up to their capacity, which is probably well beyond what the spell delivers.
  • Small flames such as candles go out after 1 segment. Small fires slow and smoke for 1 round after the rain stops. Large fires are not materially affected.

Temperature: above 90° F. the duration doubles, except in arid regions. Between 33° and 31° F. it falls as sleet. At 30° F. and below it falls as fairly thick snow, and most wetness effects are cancelled or postponed until the snow melts.

Magic: large-area magical heat (wall of fire, fireball, flame strike, etc.) applied to the rain makes a cloud of warm fog twice the area of the precipitation. Magical cold applied to the rain, or to the water left afterwards, makes normal ice.

Component: a pinch of silver dust.

The recipient gains the benefit of a bless spell and 1-8 extra hit points, both lasting as long as the aid spell. These can take the character above his or her normal full total. Damage taken while the spell lasts comes off the extra hit points first. Extra hit points from aid that are lost cannot be restored by curative magic.

Example: a 1st-level fighter with 8 hit points takes 2 points of damage, then receives aid for 6 extra hit points. He now has 12 hit points, 6 of them temporary. If he then takes 7 points of damage, he loses all 6 temporary points and 1 regular point.

Components: a tiny strip of white cloth with a sticky substance (such as tree sap) on the ends, and the cleric’s holy symbol.

Tells the cleric whether a target creature is alive. It detects life in someone under feign death, in a coma, a deathlike trance or suspended animation, and in the body of a creature that is travelling astrally. It works on plants and plant creatures as well as animals.

More than a one-inch thickness of wood or stone between cleric and subject shortens the range: each inch of wood or stone counts as 10 feet of open space. Metal of any thickness, or any form of mental protection (psionic or magical), ruins the spell without detecting anything. The spell detects the first living creature along the cleric’s line of sight (within range), or else the first creature to cross that line before the spell ends.

Conjures a weak air elemental, a dust devil: AC 4, 2 HD, MV 18˝, 1 attack for 1-4 points of damage. It can be hit by normal weapons, and magic weapons of any type do it double damage. It looks like a small whirlwind 5 feet across at the base, 15 feet tall and 10 feet across at the top. It moves as the cleric directs, but is dispelled if sent more than 3˝ from the caster.

  • Gases: its winds can hold a gas cloud, or a creature in gaseous form, at bay or push it away from the caster (but cannot damage or dispel it).
  • Flames: it puts out torches, small campfires, exposed lanterns and other small open flames of non-magical origin.
  • Dust cloud: skimming over loose dust, sand or ash, it raises a cloud 30 feet across centred on itself. Normal vision cannot see through it, and creatures inside are effectively blinded until one round after they get out.
  • Spell casting: virtually impossible inside such a cloud or inside the dust devil itself; even if its buffeting winds do no damage, a spell caster must save versus spell or lose concentration (and the spell).

Any creature native to the Elemental Plane of Air (even another dust devil) can dismiss it at will from 3˝ or less. Creatures not native to the caster’s current plane are not affected by it. It is automatically dispelled on touching any creature with innate magic resistance, but only after it has had its chance to hit and do damage.

The cleric binds and enthralls an audience that fully understands his or her language. Listeners of the cleric’s race get a saving throw versus spell; those of a race generally unfriendly to the cleric’s save at +4. Characters or creatures with more than 4 levels or hit dice, or wisdom above 15, cannot be enthralled.

The caster must speak without interruption for a full round. The spell then lasts as long as the cleric keeps talking, up to 6 turns. Those who fail their save see the cleric as having charisma 21 (loyalty base +70%, reaction adjustment +50%). They stand and listen, but do not act on the words as they would on a suggestion. When the cleric stops talking, they regain control of their minds.

The spell ends instantly if anyone attacks the cleric (a successful hit or a spell cast at him or her), or if the cleric tries to cast another spell or do anything else. Listeners who save see the cleric as having charisma 3, and may (50% chance) hoot and jeer, giving others a new saving throw. If the cleric tries to take unfair advantage by preaching a religion or alignment opposed to the audience’s, each “offended” listener gets a new saving throw at +5.

Prepares a cleric’s holy symbol, or makes a new one to replace one lost or damaged. The new symbol is the material component (and is obviously not used up). It must be made of the proper material for the religion/deity and be of the proper shape and design; a cleric cannot turn just any item into a holy symbol. A cleric may have two holy symbols at a time, so the spell can make a spare. No cleric can make a holy symbol for a religion or deity other than his or her own. A good or evil cleric’s symbol radiates a faint aura of good or evil, but is not a magic item as such; a neutral cleric’s (with respect to good and evil) has no aura.

Calls a small (size S) creature of at least animal intelligence to serve as the cleric’s messenger. It does not work on “giant” types, or on creatures with intelligence 4 or higher (or rated low intelligence or better). If such an animal is within range, the cleric lures it with some food it likes. The animal gets a saving throw versus spell; if it succeeds, the spell fails. If it fails, the animal comes to the cleric and awaits instructions.

The cleric can communicate crudely with it, telling it to go to a certain place, but directions must be simple. A small item or note can be attached to it. If told to, it waits at the destination until the spell ends, then returns to its normal life. (Unless the person meant to receive the message is expecting a small animal or bird messenger, the carrier may be ignored.) The receiver gains no ability to communicate with the animal.

The cleric changes the flow of time for himself or herself: while 1 segment passes for everyone else, the cleric spends 1 round in contemplation. The base duration is 2 segments (2 rounds, from the cleric’s point of view), plus 1 more per level: at 5th level the caster could spend up to 6 rounds thinking while only 6 segments pass for others. (The DM must allow 1 minute of real time per segment for the player to ponder a problem or question, with no discussion with unaffected characters.)

While withdrawn, the cleric can only cast augury, curing or healing spells, or informational spells, and only on himself or herself; casting any of them another way (such as cure light wounds on a companion) ends the withdraw spell. The cleric cannot walk or run, become invisible, or do anything but think, read and the like. Others can still affect the cleric, and any successful attack on him or her breaks the spell.

Named for the vague, wyvern-like haze it creates, this spell usually guards an area against intruders. Any creature that comes within 1˝ of the guarded area may be attacked: the “wyvern” strikes, and the target must save versus spell or stand paralyzed for 1 round per level of the caster, or until freed by the caster, dispel magic or remove paralysis. A successful save means the wyvern-form missed, and the spell stays in place. Once it strikes a target successfully, the paralysis takes effect and the spell’s force is used up. The spell also fades if no intruder has been struck within 8 hours of casting.

A creature approaching the guarded space may notice the haze before getting close enough to be attacked: 90% chance in bright light, 30% in twilight, 0% in darkness.

Component: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol.

The air instantly drops all its water vapor as huge raindrops, and the condensation draws in more vapor to fall as well: a true downpour. Everything in the area is drenched within 1 segment, since rain falls at 1/10 inch per segment (1 inch per round).

Normal fires in the area are put out: small ones instantly, medium-sized ones in 3-5 segments, large ones in 8-10 segments.

Magical fires are put out too, with these general rules:

  • Permanent magical fires re-light in 1-2 rounds. Small magical fires that can be re-kindled, such as a flame tongue sword’s, are affected only during the actual cloudburst.
  • Spells such as produce fire and burning hands are negated.
  • Large-area spells such as fireball, flame strike, wall of fire, etc. are put out, but turn the rain into a cloud of steam four times the spell’s area (a cylinder of up to 12˝ in diameter and as much as 24˝ high). The steam does 1-3 points of damage per round to normal creatures in it, and twice that to cold-dwelling or cold-using creatures. It lasts 2-5 rounds, half that in a breeze, or only 1 round in a strong wind.

Climate: in arid regions the spell acts only as a double-strength precipitation. In hot, humid areas the duration extends to 2 rounds. Between 33° and 31° F. inclusive, sleet falls instead, forming ice and slush as it builds up. At 30° F. and lower it becomes a snowburst, one inch of snow falling per segment.

Components: powdered silver and powdered iodine crystals, plus the cleric’s holy symbol.

The cleric touches a human or demi-human who is unconscious and “at death’s door” (−1 to −9 hit points), immediately bringing him or her to 0 hit points. The subject stays unconscious, but bleeding and deterioration stop for the spell’s duration. Now at 0 hit points, the subject can be brought round and have hit points restored by cure light wounds, cure serious wounds, etc., by potions such as healing or extra-healing, or by clerical or other items that magically restore hit points.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol, a bit of white linen and any form of unguent.

The caster, or another creature of man-size and similar mass, can withstand non-magical fires up to 2,000° F. and gains +2 on saving throws against magical fires.

For every level of the caster above the minimum needed for the spell (5th), one more man-sized creature can be protected, allowing several individuals, or one or more larger ones, to be affected. For instance, an 11th-level caster could protect himself or herself and a horse, and ride through molten lava. (A horse counts as 6 humans for this spell; a halfling-sized creature counts as ½ human, and a pixie-sized one as ¼ human.)

Components: at least 500 gp of powdered ruby and the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol.

Enchants the caster’s vestment to protect like armor, but only while the cleric is on ground consecrated to his or her deity (cf. the 1st-level ceremony spell). If the cleric wears any armor or protective device, the vestment protects as normal chain mail. If no other protection is worn, the vestment also gains +1 for every four levels of the cleric, up to chain mail +4 (base AC 1). It lasts 6 rounds per level of the caster, or until the caster falls unconscious or leaves the consecrated area.

Components: the vestment to be enchanted and the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol.

The cleric and his or her worn or carried possessions merge into a large stone. The cleric stands next to the stone, which must be big enough to hold his or her body in all three dimensions, holding a small sample of the same kind of stone. When the casting ends, the cleric and up to 100 pounds of non-living gear blend into the stone. Magical artifacts and relics are not affected. If the stone is too small, or the cleric has more than 100 pounds of gear, the spell fails and is wasted.

Duration: 9-16 (1d8 + 8) rounds; the DM rolls the variable part in secret. Before it ends, the cleric can step out through the same surface used to enter (the spell gives no movement through the stone, unlike passwall or phase door). If the duration runs out first, the cleric is expelled and takes 4-32 (4d8) points of damage, and each item of affected gear must save versus petrification or turn to stone.

Inside, the cleric is aware of time passing, but cannot see or hear anything outside.

Spells cast on the occupied stone: stone to flesh expels the cleric with 4-32 points of damage (but carried items need not save); stone shape does 4-16 (4d4) points of damage but does not expel the cleric; transmute rock to mud expels the cleric and kills him or her instantly unless a saving throw versus spell succeeds.

rolls.label: Expelled when the time runs out, or by stone to flesh

system.description:
Partly protects the caster, or another eligible creature touched, against undead that exist on the Negative Material Plane (such as a shadow, wight, wraith, spectre or vampire). The spell opens a channel to the Positive Material Plane whose energy offsets the undead’s attack.

When an undead creature touches (attacks) the recipient, the recipient saves versus death magic:

  • Success: normal hit-point damage, but no experience drain, and the undead takes 2-12 (2d6) hit points of damage from the Positive Plane energy.
  • Failure: double the usual physical damage, plus the normal loss of experience.

The protection works against only one such attack and then ends, whether the save succeeds or not. It also protects against a magic-user’s energy drain spell, though then the magic-user is not harmed. The contact between the planes makes a bright flash and a sound like a thunderclap, but these do no damage. It lasts 1 turn per level of the cleric, or until the recipient is successfully attacked by an undead monster. It cannot be cast on the Negative Material Plane.

rolls.label: Undead struck by Positive Plane energy

system.description:
Frees creatures from paralysis or similar effects (such as a hold spell). The cleric casts it and points, affecting up to 4 creatures within range and the area of effect. There must be no physical or magical barrier between caster and targets, or the spell fails and is wasted. Each target gets a new saving throw versus paralyzation: +3 if only one creature is targeted, +2 for two, +1 for three or four.

Reverse (cause paralysis): affects only one target, which the cleric must touch with his or her holy/unholy symbol (a successful roll “to hit”). If it fails a saving throw versus spell, it is paralyzed for 1-6 rounds plus 1 round per level of the caster. Good clerics should be very careful about using it, and some good-aligned orders may forbid it.

The caster, or another creature of man-size and similar mass, can walk on water as if it were firm, grassy ground (cf. ring of water walking). For every level of the caster above the minimum for the spell (5th level), one more man-sized creature can be affected, allowing several individuals, or one or more larger ones. For instance, an 11th-level caster could also affect a horse and ride over the waves. (A horse counts as 6 humans for this spell.)

Components: a piece of cork and the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol.

Tries to send a creature from another plane back to its own. The cleric must know the exact name of the creature’s type, and its specific (proper) name if it has one. The chance of success is figured as for dispel magic: base 50%, plus or minus the difference between the caster’s level and the creature’s level/HD. Roll percentile dice; a roll equal to or less than the chance sends the creature instantly back to its own plane. Otherwise the spell fails. (A creature that does not want to stay on the caster’s plane may be grateful for the attempt.)

Reverse (implore): asks some like-aligned creature from another plane to come to the cleric. Success is figured as for abjure, and again the caster must know the exact name of the creature’s type and its given name, if any. Even if it works, there is no guarantee the creature will be friendly.

Neither version works on deities, but either might affect their servants or minions.

Components: a holy/unholy symbol, holy or unholy water, and often some material hateful to the creature. For implore, the last is replaced by something the creature craves or respects.

The cleric radiates an aura of fear out to a 3’ radius. Any character or creature that enters it must save versus spell or run away in fear for 6 rounds (cf. the 3rd-level magic-user spell fear). Once one creature fails its save, the spell ends. It does not affect creatures that radiate fear themselves or any kind of undead, and their contact does not end it; nor does an intruder who saves. Otherwise it lasts 1 turn per level of the cleric. The cleric’s own party is not immune. The cleric can cancel the aura at any time.

Reverse (cloak of bravery): cast on the cleric or another willing creature, it gives +3 on the saving throw against any one form of magical fear. It works only once, on one figure, and ends whether or not that save succeeds. It does not stop a creature (such as a devil) from radiating fear, so the creature can still affect others nearby.

Components: for cloak of fear, a miniature quiver and a chicken feather; for cloak of bravery, a drop of alcohol and the brain of a newt.

Turns one or more normal insects into larger forms like the “giant” versions in the MM and MMII or the FF. Only actual insects are affected, not arachnids, crustaceans or other small creatures, and only one type of insect per casting (not an ant and a fly together).

Cleric levelNumber of insectsTotal hit dice
7th-9th13 HD
10th or 11th24 HD
12th or 13th35 HD
14th or higher46 HD

Casting time: one round per hit die of the resulting insect(s). If interrupted, the insect(s) die and the spell is ruined.

Attacks and damage: a created insect has as many attacks per round as its giant namesake, but does full damage only if it has at least as many hit dice as the usual giant version, and can never do more than the damage given in the books. A 14th-level cleric could make a 6 HD wasp (instead of the usual 4 HD giant wasp; see MM), but it would still do 2-8/1-4. A 7th-level cleric’s 3 HD giant wasp would do only 2-6/1-3, three-fourths of a “real” giant wasp’s damage, since it has three-fourths of the usual hit dice.

Created insects have none of the special attacks or defenses of standard giant forms, but their armor class, movement rate and other physical characteristics are as in the book listing. They will not try to harm the cleric, but control is limited to simple commands such as “attack,” “defend,” “guard,” and so forth; they cannot be told to attack a certain creature or guard against a particular event. Unless told otherwise, they attack whoever or whatever is near them.

Reverse (shrink insect): shrinks standard giant insects as well as those made by this spell, by 1 HD per 4 levels of the cleric, up to 6 HD of reduction (to a minimum of 1/8 HD, or 1 hp). Special attacks are kept, but weaker, giving a bonus on the saving throw against them. For instance, a 9th-level cleric could shrink a standard giant wasp from 4 HD to 1 HD; it could still use its poison sting, but saves against it would be at +3 (or perhaps higher), and its damage would drop to 1-2 for a bite and 1 point for a sting, one-fourth of normal, since it is one-fourth its original size.

Component: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol, for either version.

Gives a character who normally cannot cast spells the ability to cast particular spells. It works only on thieves, fighters, cavaliers, assassins, monks, rangers (under 8th level) and paladins (under 9th level), not on any other class or sub-class, any monster, or anyone with less than one full hit die. The recipient must have wisdom 9 or higher.

Which spells: only spells the cleric currently has memorized (prayed for), and only informational or defensive spells, or cure light wounds. Trying to transfer any other kind makes the whole spell fail, so no spells are imbued even if other allowed ones were chosen. Up to three spells can be imbued: one 2nd-level spell and one or two 1st-level spells. Any eligible recipient can receive one 1st-level spell; the recipient must be at least 3rd level for two 1st-level spells, and at least 5th level for a 2nd-level spell.

Spell details that vary with caster level (range, duration, area, etc.) use the recipient’s level; all other details (casting time, components, etc.) apply normally.

The cleric loses the transferred spells and cannot memorize more spells until the recipient has used all of them.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol, plus some minor item “borrowed” from the recipient that symbolizes his or her profession (a lock pick for a thief, a dagger for an assassin, etc.), which is used up in the casting.

The cleric, or any creature touched, becomes immune to one specified spell of 4th level or lower that the cleric has personally experienced (if the cleric has been hit by a fireball, for instance, the spell can protect someone from fireballs). It protects only against that particular spell, not a class or group of similar spells: someone immune to lightning bolt is still vulnerable to shocking grasp. It protects against actually cast spells only, not magic items or creatures’ innate spell-like abilities, but the immunity lasts the full duration.

It cannot be cast on someone already magically protected by a spell or other temporary effect. Only one spell immunity can be on a creature at a time; later castings do nothing until the first one ends. Items the recipient carries are not protected and must still save (if applicable).

Component: the same as for the spell being protected against (if any).

Useful wherever there is plant growth of moderate size or density. Ground-covering plants and/or roots and rootlets become very hard and sharply pointed. The ground looks unchanged, but acts as if strewn with caltrops; on bare ground or earthen pits, roots and rootlets act the same way.

Without true seeing, similar magic, or some other special detection (such as detect traps), the area is completely undetectable until a victim enters it and is hurt, and even then the victim cannot tell how far it extends without magical detection.

For each 1˝ of movement through the area, a victim suffers 2 “attacks”, rolled as if the caster were attacking; each hit does 1-4 points of damage. Spells that control or harm plants, or dispel magic, negate the area.

Components: the cleric’s holy symbol and either seven sharp thorns or seven small twigs, each sharpened to a point.

The recipient can walk on air as if it were solid ground. Climbing is like walking up a hill: the steeper, the slower. A 45° climb is at one-half normal movement, 60° at one-fourth, and straight up at one-eighth. Descent can be fast, like running downhill: invert those proportions, so straight down can be up to eight times normal speed (or any slower rate wanted). The walker always controls his or her speed, and even when dropping fast can “stop on a copper piece” to avoid crashing into the ground or another solid object.

In the area of a gust of wind spell, an air walker moves at one-half the usual rate going into the gust, or twice the usual rate going with it.

The spell can be put on any creature touched, up to and including one of giant size. The caster could, for example, put it on a trained horse and ride through the air, but an animal not used to this would panic, so it would need careful, lengthy training.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol and a bit of thistledown.

Animates 1 humanoid or semi-humanoid skeleton or corpse for every 2 levels of the caster, who can then command them. They obey direct commands or instructions of up to about 12 words (cf. animate dead).

What can be animated: including but not limited to apes (carnivorous and giant), bugbears, ettins, giants (all varieties), ogres and trolls (all varieties). In general, the remains must be of two-legged monsters of more than 3 hit dice, with skeletons like a human’s except in size, which must be over 7’ tall.

Statistics: animated corpses are monster zombies (see MMII), or normal (living) creatures of the same form if that creature normally has less than 6 hit dice. Animated skeletons have half the normal creature’s hit dice (rounded up). Both keep their normal physical attacks, but have no special attacks or defenses beyond those of monster zombies or skeletons.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol and a small specimen of the type of creature to be animated.

The cleric must first personally build the golem’s form and cast a prayer spell on it. All golems are man-shaped and roughly man-sized, from 3’ to 7’ tall. The kind of golem depends on the material and the cleric’s level:

Golem (minimum level)Build timeDurationStatisticsCarries
Straw (9th)1 hour1 hour/levelAC 10, MV 12˝, HD 2 + 4, hp 20, #AT 2, D 1-2/1-2; SD immune to piercing weapons, half damage from blunt weapons; takes double damage from flame30 pounds

These are called lesser golems, to tell them apart from the golems in the MM. Like those, they are mindless, so charm, fear, hold, sleep and the like do not affect them. A lesser golem saves as a cleric of its creator’s level. It cannot speak, but understands and carries out simple instructions of no more than a dozen words.

Makes a holy/unholy water font into a scrying device, much like a crystal ball (see DMG, Miscellaneous Magic Treasure, crystal ball). It only works if the cleric is in good standing with his or her deity. The cleric can scry for 1 round per vial the basin holds, so the duration depends on the size of the font. For the chance that a character notices being scried on, see the crystal ball in the DMG and the magic-user spell magic mirror herein.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol and the font and its trappings, none of which are used up.

The cleric must be in sight of a rainbow of any kind, or have a special component (see below). The cleric chooses one of four uses when casting:

Bow: a shimmering, many-layered bow of rainbow colors, light and easy to draw, usable by anyone with strength 6 or better, but only by a character class allowed to use bows. There is no non-proficiency penalty. It fires 7 missiles, each counting as a +3 weapon, once or twice per round as the user wishes, and then disappears. When it is drawn, an arrow of the chosen color appears nocked and ready, and that color leaves the bow. If no color is named, or one already used is asked for, the next color in spectrum order appears. Each color does double damage to certain creatures:

  • Red: fire dwellers/users
  • Orange: earth elementals
  • Yellow: plant targets (including fungus creatures, shambling mounds, treants, etc.)
  • Green: aquatic creatures and water elementals
  • Blue: aerial creatures, electricity-using creatures and air elementals
  • Indigo: acid-using or poison-using creatures
  • Violet: metallic or regenerating creatures

Bridge: a seven-colored bridge, as many feet wide as the cleric has levels, bearing as many hundreds of pounds as the cleric has levels. It is 20’ to 120’ long, as the caster wishes. If its weight limit is ever exceeded, it simply vanishes; otherwise it lasts for the spell’s duration or until the caster dismisses it.

Elevator: the rainbow lifts the caster and everyone within a 10’ radius skyward along an upward arc, as high as the cleric wants, and down again if desired, at 12˝; the arc trails 12˝ behind the travelers. They must reach a safe place before the spell ends, or the rainbow vanishes beneath them.

Flagon: the rainbow condenses into a seven-colored vessel holding seven measures of pure water. As each measure is poured, one of the vessel’s colors mixes with it to make a magical draught, with the effect of the spell cast by a 12th level cleric (the effects last after the spell ends). Unused measures vanish with the vessel when the spell ends.

  • Red: cure light wounds
  • Orange: resist fire
  • Yellow: cure blindness
  • Green: slow poison
  • Blue: cure disease
  • Indigo: resist cold
  • Violet: remove paralysis

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol and a vial of holy/unholy water. If no rainbow is near, the cleric can use instead a diamond worth at least 1,000 gp, prepared earlier in sight of a rainbow by casting bless and prayer on it. Only the holy symbol remains after casting.

system.aoe: 1˝ square per level, 1 spike per 1' sq.
system.description:
Rock, natural or worked, shapes itself into long sharp points that blend into the background, slowing movement through the area or causing damage. Each person who observes the area carefully is 25% likely to notice the points.

Otherwise, creatures entering the area are attacked as soon as they set foot in it and at each step afterwards; each spike that hits does 1-4 points of damage, with hits rolled as if the caster were fighting. The first step only alerts a victim if that first attack hits; otherwise the victim keeps moving and the spikes go unnoticed until damage is done. After first taking damage, running or charging victims suffer 2 attacks per 1˝ of movement rate over the area before they can stop; others suffer only 1 more attack-like check.

Those falling into a pit lined with spike stones suffer 6 attack-like checks, each at +2 “to hit” and +2 damage for each 10’ fallen, in addition to normal falling damage.

Component: four tiny stalactites.

Can only be used to secure a consecrated area (cf. ceremony). Its effect on those trying to enter depends on their ethics (law/chaos) and morals (good/evil) compared with the caster’s:

  • Identical morals and ethics: cannot enter unless the password is known (no saving throw).
  • Different ethics: save versus spell to enter; on a failure, take 2-12 points of damage.
  • Different morals: save versus spell to enter; on a failure, take 4-24 points of damage.

An intruder who fails a saving throw can never enter the area until the spell ends. Effects are cumulative, so several saving throws may well be needed. Intruders who get in by making their saves still feel uneasy and tense. The caster is immune.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol, holy/unholy water, silver/dung, and iron/sulfur.

system.aoe: One individual per level of caster
system.description:
Creates a great feast for as many creatures as the cleric has levels, with a magnificent table, chairs, service and all the food and drink needed. Eating it takes one full hour, and the benefits begin only after that hour. If the feast is interrupted for any reason, the spell is ruined and all its effects are lost.

  • The nectar-like drink cures all diseases, gives immunity to poison for 12 hours, and heals 5-8 points of damage.
  • The ambrosia-like food acts as a bless lasting 12 hours.
  • For those 12 hours, the diners are also immune to fear, hopelessness and panic.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol and specially fermented honey taken from the cells of bee larvae destined to be queens.

The cleric confronts a powerful creature from another plane (such as a deva or a powerful “name” demon, but not a demigod or deity of any kind) and demands some duty or quest from it. The creature cannot be ethically or morally opposed to the cleric (not evil if the cleric is good, not chaotic if the cleric is lawful). A true neutral creature counts as strongly opposed to good and evil, and to law and chaos.

Grounds for service: the cleric must know something about the creature that justifies the demand, such as a favor it once received from someone of the cleric’s alignment, or else must pledge some valuable gift or service in return. The service demanded must be reasonable compared with that past or promised favor. The spell then acts as a quest on the creature.

Payment: as soon as the service is done, the creature is transported to the cleric, who must then and there pay what was promised, whether by permanently cancelling a past debt or by giving some service or material reward. The creature is then instantly free to return to its own plane. If the cleric does not keep the promise to the letter, at the very least the cleric becomes subject to exaction by the creature or its master, liege, etc. At worst, the creature may attack the cleric, completely immune to all of that cleric’s spells for breaking the bargain.

Components: the cleric’s holy/unholy symbol, some matter or substance from the creature’s plane, and the cleric’s knowledge of the creature’s nature and/or actions written on a parchment leaf, which is burned to seal the bargain.

The cleric places a powerful dweomer in a specially prepared object (a string of prayer beads, a small clay tablet, an ivory baton, etc.), which then radiates magic. The cleric must willingly give it to someone and tell him or her its command word. When the holder speaks the word while breaking the item, he or she, with everything worn and carried, is instantly transported to the cleric’s sanctuary as if by word of recall. No other creatures are affected.

Reverse: when the item is broken and the word spoken, the cleric is transported to the holder’s immediate vicinity. The cleric can refuse this “summons” at the instant it happens, but then the chance is gone forever and the spell is wasted.

Preparing the item costs 2,000 to 5,000 gold pieces for either version.

Like the cleric spell of the same name, with several uses in the druid hierarchy. It leaves no aura of magic, though know alignment or similar magic might reveal the force of true neutrality involved. The ceremonies and their levels are listed below (the UA text says each can be cast “by a druid of the indicated or lower level”):

  • 1st-level druid: coming of age, rest eternal, marriage
  • 3rd-level druid: dedication, investiture
  • 7th-level druid: initiation, special vows
  • 9th-level druid: hallowed ground
  • 12th-level druid: cast out

Coming of age: performed on young people in druidic societies, usually at age 14, marking their entrance into adulthood. The effect is the same as the cleric version ( +1 bonus on a single saving throw); see the cleric text for other details.

Rest eternal: cast on a dead body to speed the soul/spirit on its journey to its final resting place. Raise dead and resurrection cannot then bring the character back to life, though a wish could.

Marriage: essentially the same as the cleric ceremony.

Dedication: takes the recipient into the ranks of the druid’s followers/worshipers, if the character is true neutral. The recipient, like druids, is charged with preserving and protecting nature and the balance of forces in the world. Otherwise similar to the cleric ceremony.

Investiture: must be performed on a character before he or she can become an Aspirant (1st-level druid). It gives no other benefit.

Initiation: gives the druid the shape-changing power and immunity to woodland charm that become available at 7th level. It must be performed right after the druid begins advancing through 7th level; cast earlier, it does not work, and the druid lacks those powers until initiated. Usually another druid of 7th or higher level performs it, but in unusual cases a druid may cast it on himself or herself.

Special vows: works like the cleric rite. It does not work on paladins, but works on cavaliers of any alignment.

Hallowed ground: cast on the druid’s permanent grove, so that its trees are never affected by disease or other natural disasters, for as long as the druid keeps the grove as his or her permanent base.

Cast out: excommunication or punishment for someone who has committed sacrilege against nature or otherwise violated the principles and standards of druidism. The cast-out character gives off a powerful negative aura, so natural creatures react badly to him or her: all normal (non-magical) animals, woodland monsters, domestic beasts such as horses and dogs, and all druids and their followers. A reversed version of the ceremony, by the same druid or another of at least as high a level, can later lessen the effect, but only a Hierophant Druid (of any level) can completely remove it.

Cast out is so severe that a druid needs permission from his or her Archdruid to perform it; an Archdruid needs permission from the Great Druid, and the Great Druid from the Grand Druid. The Grand Druid needs no permission, but a Hierophant Druid can reverse his or her actions at any time. It is used only when an offense is serious enough to deserve it; a druid who asks and is refused, or whose casting is later reversed by another druid, may be punished by higher-ranking members of the hierarchy. An unwilling target saves versus spell at −4 to negate it.

Components: always mistletoe. Every ceremony must be performed in a druid grove or some other natural, healthy patch of forest, normally at dawn or dusk, when night and day are in balance.

system.aoe: One object or creature per round
system.description:
Tells the druid whether non-neutral forces and alignments are at work in the object or creature examined. A partly neutral alignment (such as a neutral good cleric’s) gives a mild aura; one with no neutral part (such as a chaotic good fighter’s) gives a strong aura. It does not reveal the exact alignment, only that it is not true neutral: a paladin and a chaotic evil thief give the same aura at the same strength. A true neutral subject (such as another druid) gives a smooth, well-balanced aura recognizable as neutrality.

It does not work on non-living items without a natural aura (such as a vial of poison), but does work on an object such as an aligned magical sword. Creatures under an unknowable alignment spell or similar magic show no aura.

The druid can tell whether an object, creature or area contains poison or has been poisoned. Each check covers about 1 cubic yard, so the druid cannot tell if a whole pond is poisoned, but can tell if the part scanned that round (or something in it) contains poison. Several areas can be checked during the spell.

There is also a 5% chance per level of the caster of learning the type of poison: contact (insinuative), ingestive or respirative (gas). A single failure on this roll makes the spell useless for finding poison types for the rest of that casting, so trying it on every area is nearly pointless.

Components: mistletoe and a yew leaf, which turns brown if poison is present, so several may be needed to use the whole duration.
Identical to the 1st-level cleric spell of the same name, except that the druid also needs mistletoe as a material component.

A blazing, blade-like ray of red-hot fire springs from the druid’s hand, wielded as if it were a scimitar. A hit does 5-8 points of damage: +2 against undead or creatures especially vulnerable to fire, −2 against creatures protected from fire, and none at all against fire-dwellers or creatures that use fire as an attack. It ignites combustibles such as parchment, straw, dry sticks, cloth, etc. It counts as a magical weapon only against undead, so creatures that can only be hit by magical weapons are not harmed unless they are undead.

Components: mistletoe and a leaf of sumac.

Cast on a handful of freshly picked berries, it makes 2 to 8 of them magical. The caster (and any other druid of 3rd or higher level) can tell at once which ones; detect magic also reveals them. Each magical berry either nourishes a hungry man-sized creature as well as a full normal meal, or cures 1 point of damage from wounds or similar causes, up to a maximum of 8 points of such curing in any 24-hour period.

Reverse (badberry): rotten berries look wholesome, but each eaten does 1 point of poison damage (no saving throw).

Component: mistletoe passed over the freshly picked edible berries (blueberries, blackberries, raspberries, currants, gooseberries, etc.).

Turns a pool of normal water in a natural setting, no more than 2 feet across per level of the caster, into a scrying device like a crystal ball, much as the magic-user spell magic mirror and the cleric spell magic font (both described elsewhere in this text) do. It can only scry planes coexistent with or bordering the Prime Material Plane, that is, the Inner Planes (including the Para-elemental Planes, Plane of Shadow, et al.). The penalties for scrying beyond the druid’s own plane given for the crystal ball (see DMG) apply.

Detect magic, detect snares and pits and detect poison can be cast through the pool, each with a 5% per level chance of working correctly. Infravision and ultravision work normally through it, as do starshine and moonbeam (see hereafter).

Components: mistletoe, and refined oil pressed from nuts such as hickory and walnut, dropped in three measures onto the pool (a measure need be no more than an ounce).

Identical to the 2nd-level cleric spell slow poison, except that if the druid can tell the poison was made from a living plant, he or she has a 5% chance per level of knowing an herbal antidote that neutralizes it. (If the Dungeon Master does not say what the poison is, a successful detect poison [type] showing an organic poison means it can be countered.) A roll equal to or less than this chance neutralizes the poison.

Components: mistletoe, and crushed garlic rubbed on the recipient’s feet. Antidotes must come from green plants outdoors, or from an herbalist or similar supplier.

Essentially the same as the 3rd-level cleric spell of the same name, except that lightning cannot be called with it, call lightning cannot be used in the same area at the same time, and the druid needs mistletoe as an extra material component.

Essentially the same as the 2nd-level cleric spell of the same name, except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and this one: because of the shorter duration, it can examine at most five creatures. It cannot be reversed.

Essentially the same as the 4th-level cleric spell of the same name, except for the differences given in the spell’s statistics and these: the area radiates an aura of magic, and detect snares and pits reveals where the spike growth is. The druid uses mistletoe (instead of the cleric’s holy symbol) along with the seven small twigs or thorns.

Softly lights an area as if under a clear night sky full of stars, whatever the height of the open space above it. Vision is clear to 30’, unclear out to 60’, and beyond that only gleams and glimmers can be made out. Shadows are cast. Ultravision works to its full potential, but infravision is not affected. The area seems to have a real night sky; disbelieving the illusion only reveals that the “stars” are conjured lights.

Components: several stalks from an amaryllis (especially Hypoxis) and several holly berries.

A beam of soft, pale light shines down from above onto whatever area the druid points at. It is exactly like moonlight, so no colors can be told apart except shades of black, gray and white. The caster can easily move it to any area he or she can see and point to, so it is a good way to spotlight something, such as an opponent; though it allows shadows, a creature in the center of the beam is certainly being watched. Reflected light allows dim vision 1˝ beyond the area. It does not hinder infravision, and brings ultravision to its greatest potential.

Components: several seeds of any moonseed plant and a piece of opalescent feldspar (moonstone).

system.aoe: 1˝ square per level, 1 spike per 1' sq.
system.description: The same as the 5th-level cleric spell of the same name.

The druid enchants a healthy oak to serve as a protector. Only one tree at a time: while one of the druid’s liveoaks is active, he or she cannot cast another. The tree must be within 10 feet of the druid’s home, within a place sacred to the druid, or within 10˝ of something the druid wants guarded. It can be a small, medium or large tree, as wished and available.

The druid places a “trigger” phrase on it of up to one word per level of the caster. For instance, “Attack any persons who come near without first saying ‘sacred mistletoe’ ” is an 11-word trigger a druid of 11th or higher level could use. When triggered, the tree becomes a treant of matching size and attack ability, as in the MM, but with only a 3˝ movement rate.

The oak radiates a magic aura, and returns to normal if dispel magic succeeds or the druid wishes it. Component: mistletoe.

Water in the area instantly turns to powdery dust. If the water is already muddy, the area is doubled; if it is wet mud, the area is quadrupled. Water that stays in contact with the dust quickly soaks into it, turning it into silty mud if there is enough water, or otherwise wetting it.

Only liquid in the area at the moment of casting is affected. Liquids that are only partly water lose their water content, and potions containing water become useless. Living creatures are unaffected, except those native to the Elemental Plane of Water: such a creature saves versus spell to escape, and only one can be affected per casting, whatever its size or the size of the area.

Reverse: simply a very powerful create water spell, needing a pinch of normal dust as an extra component.

Components (either version): diamond dust worth at least 500 gp, a bit of seashell and the druid’s mistletoe.

The druid’s staff of dead wood becomes a treant of the largest size.

Making the staff: the druid must find a tree struck by lightning within the past 24 hours (1%-5% chance for any given tree, depending on how severe the storm was), take a sound limb, and prepare a specially cured section, shaped and carved to receive the magic. It must be ash, oak or yew. Curing by sun drying and special smoke takes 28 days; shaping, carving, smoothing and polishing take another 28 days; the druid cannot adventure or do other strenuous things during either period. The finished staff, carved with scenes of woodland life, is rubbed with holly berry juice, and its end is pushed into the earth of the druid’s grove while the druid speaks with plants, asking the staff to help in time of need. It is then charged with a dweomer that lasts for many changes from staff to treant and back.

Hit dice: the treant starts at 12 hit dice and 96 hit points, and each 8 points of damage it takes reduces it by 1 hit die: 11 and 88, 10 and 80, 9 and 72, etc. As it loses hit dice it shrinks, losing attack power too. If it drops below 7 hit dice it crumbles to sawdust-like powder and is lost. Only a wish can restore it (completely); otherwise a new staff can be found, seasoned and so on, to start again.

Use: when the druid plants the staff in the ground and speaks a special command prayer and invocation, it becomes a treant that defends the druid and obeys him or her in any way. It is not a true treant and cannot talk with real treants. It lasts as many turns as the druid has levels, until the druid orders it back to its true form, or until it is destroyed, whichever comes first.

Components: mistletoe, or leaves (ash, oak or yew) of the same kind as the staff.

The druid calls up a burning beam of light, like real sunlight in every important way.

  • Blindness: all creatures in the area are blinded for 1-3 rounds unless they save versus spell. Creatures using ultravision at the time may be blinded for 2-8 rounds. Creatures to whom sunlight is harmful or unnatural are blinded permanently, or for 2-12 rounds if they save.
  • Infravision: creatures in the area, and within 2˝ of its edge, lose infravision for 2-5 rounds.
  • Undead (including vampires) in the main area take 8-48 points of damage, or half on a successful save versus spell. Those in the secondary area (up to 2˝ beyond the edge) take 3-18, or none on a successful save.
  • Fungi: the ultraviolet light damages fungoid creatures and subterranean fungi as if they were undead, with no saving throw.

Components: an aster seed and a piece of aventurine feldspar (sunstone).

rolls.label: Blinded on a save, harmed by sunlight (rounds)
Undead within 2" of the perimeter (none on a save)

system.description: Makes non-living liquid or solid material about 40° F. cooler, but not below freezing. The chill lasts only an instant, then the material slowly warms back to normal. Components: a soft whistle (verbal) and a downward-thrust thumb (somatic).

Removes heavy soil, dirt and similar foreign matter from floors, walls, dishes, windows, etc., leaving them spotless. Care is needed not to remove pigments and the like, so usually only one type of material is treated per use. Components: a low outrush of air and a circular hand motion.

Brings color to an object: restoring faded hues, or tinting an already colored thing a different hue. Dull or faded fabric can be brightened, pigments restored, or even hair or skin changed to another color. The effect must be renewed every 30 days. Components: a humming and a back-and-forth or wringing hand motion.

Fills the area with a fog-like dampness that leaves everything in it damp to the touch. It has many uses. It is hard on parchment, and likewise makes it and similar materials hard to set alight. Those in the area are wrapped in a light fog; objects in it stay visible but lose their detail. Components: a low hooting or hummed tune, and an upward hand gesture with writhing fingers.
Removes dampness and excess moisture from materials in the area; useful for cloth, herbs and cleaning chores. Components: a sound like that of dampen, and a two-handed wringing motion.

Removes all fine dust and tiny grit from exposed surfaces such as floors, shelves, walls, etc. The material is moved elsewhere, though new dust can of course gather. Components: a continuous indrawn breath and a back-and-forth hand motion.

Kills a small pest such as a fly, mouse, rat, beetle or the like, indoors or out. If the pests are very small, an area of up to ½ cubic foot can be cleared. It works against magical creations and normal-sized creatures magically shrunk to insect size, but not on polymorphed creatures or similarly enchanted beings. Components: a pointed finger and a low zzzt sound.

Gives food or drink a better or different flavor: mush can taste like lobster bisque. It does not change quality or wholesomeness. Spoiled food stays spoiled, and a poisoned drink is still deadly (though any telltale taste of the poison may be hidden this way). Components: a muttered lip-smacking sound and a shaking motion.

Brings new life or freshness to food and drink such as milk, beer, meat and raw vegetables, and to cut vegetables, flowers, herbs, etc. It removes a slight taint of spoilage, revives drooping flowers, and so on, but is less effective than purify food & drink and lasts only an hour. The subject must be fairly small: a small cask of liquid, a sheep, a bushel of vegetables, etc. Against a creature harmed by magic such as purify food & drink, it does 1-4 points of damage. Components: an mmmmmm sound, with the hand making a mystic sign (thumb and forefinger in a circle, the other fingers upright and apart).

Neatly gathers many small objects into a stack or pile, such as spilled nails, nuts, coins or papers. It can be selective, separating one type of material from another, but only the chosen type is gathered neatly. Components: naming the material to be gathered while making a gathering motion.

Smooths and brings a luster to wood, metal, stone, leather or ceramic. The object must be fairly clean first, and of reasonable size (a floor of up to 1,000 square feet, an armoire, etc.); it works better on smaller things such as boots, mirrors, crystal containers, etc. Components: humming a tune while making a buffing motion.

A sprinkling of fine salt appears and falls on the chosen object: a stew, a troublesome patch of weeds, a barrel of stockfish to be preserved. The object should be of reasonable size, up to perhaps 4 square yards or about 30 gallons of liquid; a smaller object may be over-salted, and a larger one will not get much. Creatures harmed by salt (such as a giant slug) take 1-4 points of damage. Components: a smacking of the lips while the hand makes a sprinkling motion.

Like polish, but removes tarnish, rust, corrosion and similar coatings, giving objects that can take it a mirror-bright, smooth, unmarred surface. A single object of up to about 1 cubic yard can be treated. A piece of jewelry is made more attractive, and its gems (only) might even become more valuable: if the gems’ base value was originally decreased, the owner may choose to find out whether shining changes it (the DM rolls again on the “Increase or Decrease of Worth Beyond Base Value” table on page 26 of the DMG, with a −1 modifier to the roll). No gem can be “re-valued” this way more than once. Components: similar to polish.

Unlike flavor, this actually produces a particular spice on the food or drink: ginger, pepper and the like for zest (or disguise), or herbs such as bay leaf, garlic, parsley and so forth. There is enough to season food or drink for about a dozen people. It appears above the dish as fine powder or flakes and falls into it. Components: humming a tune while the hand makes a crumbling and sprinkling motion.

Speeds the growth of plants, especially the germination of seeds: seeds shoot out tiny sprouts, new plants grow an inch or so, buds flower, etc. Fruits and vegetables can be made to ripen (or go past ripe to spoiled). Components: a rustling sound while the hand makes hoeing motions.

Magically sews new seams or repairs old ones in cloth or leather: about 20 yards of cloth, but only about 2 yards of leather. The seam is no stronger or weaker than a normal one. Components: usually a brief rhyme while the hand makes a sewing motion.
The same as spice, but produces a sweetener: sugar, honey or even a syrup. Components: a buzzing sound and a stirring motion.

Makes thread, string, cord, rope or even cable knot itself tightly to its own other end, or to an end of a similar object within 1’ of it. The knot is a normal one of whatever kind is wanted (square knot, half-hitch, running bowline, etc.). Components: naming the knot while holding up three fingers.

The same as chill, but warms the liquid or solid by at most about 40° F. It never makes living creatures warmer than their normal body temperature. Components: an aah sound while rubbing the hands briskly together.

Creates a strong, sturdy wrapping of suitable material and thickness around a bit of herbs, a heap of flour, a bundle of cloth, etc.: a few ounces of fine powder in waxy tissue, gems in a felt-like envelope, meal in cloth, and so forth. It can be unwrapped normally, or the caster can simply order it open, so it is often used to hold spell material components. Components: naming the general kind of wrapping wanted while making folding motions.

Affects many foods and drinks, not just milk: it curdles milk and speeds spoilage or wilting, though it does not putrefy food and drink as that spell does. Its effect is permanent. Otherwise it is like freshen. Components: a retching sound while pointing the thumb down.
The opposite of clean: soils, spots and sullies walls, floors, dishes, garments, etc. Components: a spitting sound while shuffling and stamping the feet.
A film of dust and grime settles on all exposed surfaces in the area. Components: a low humming while the hands make shaking motions.

Not one of the useful cantrips that apprentices reverse for mischief, but one generally used for no good purpose. Hair, fur or hairlike growth thickens and grows 2-12 inches longer: a head of hair, a peach, a beard, a cat, or whatever. It must be trimmed or cut to remove the effect.

It can be reversed to shorten growth, or effectively shave; but on short growth (under 1 inch) the result is no growth at all for 2-12 days, so it is not often used. Components: snicking sounds, with massaging motions for growth or scissoring motions for removal.

A variation of tie: thread, string, cord or rope ties itself in a knot that is very hard to undo, taking 2-8 rounds, less the untier’s dexterity reaction bonus. It works even on material already tied by tie, but not on magical ropes, ropes being held by a character or creature, or taut lines such as a bowstring. Components: a low zzzz sound while moving the arm forward with a strong wrist motion.

rolls.label: Time to untie (rounds, less dexterity reaction bonus)

system.description: The reverse of stitch. It works only if there is a loose or broken thread in the seam or fabric, except on material magically stitched with stitch, which it always unravels unless the item is otherwise magical (a bag of holding, a cloak of protection, boots of elvenkind, etc.). Components: saying the cantrip’s name while the fingers make a plucking motion.

Gives food or drink a sour taste, like vinegar of the appropriate sort. Usually used to spoil wine, beer or a pastry, but it can be useful: it actually produces up to about a pint of vinegar above the target, which can be an empty container where vinegar is wanted. Components: pursed lips and a whoosh sound while clenching the hand.

The opposite of gather: tips over a container so its contents spill out, if it is not securely closed or capped. The magic is weak, so containers larger than about a gallon, or magical ones, are not affected. Components: an uh-oh sound with an abrupt hand motion.

A variation of tie: fine material such as thread, hair, small grass and the like twists into a tangle, including mixes such as grass and string or hair and threads. It does not work on heavy material such as rope. Untangling takes 3-12 rounds, unless done roughly, breaking, snapping and tearing the material. Components: a buzzing while the finger makes a stirring motion.

The reverse of shine: covers an object that can tarnish with rust, corrosion, verdigris or the like. The object must be about 1 cubic yard or less. Components: a spitting sound while the hand makes a sprinkling motion.

The reverse of tie: removes a knot or tying from a chosen thread, string, cord, etc., and also undoes a tangle. It will not remove both a knot and a normal tying (a normal knot or one made by tie) at once: it removes the knot, leaving the normal tying. It has no effect on magical objects. Components: vary with the result wanted; generally a popping sound while the hands move apart, as if untying a knot or snapping a cord.

A reverse of freshen that affects only plant material, growing or picked: a plant wilts (or may wither if not very healthy), or cut flowers sag or droop. Components: a descending hum while the forefinger slowly curls down from upright.

Changes one small object into another of the same kingdom; only animal and plant objects are affected. A piece of parchment can become a brightly colored cloth square, and another change cantrip can turn the cloth into a rose; a bird can become a bat, and another can turn the bat into a flying squirrel, and so forth. Each change needs its own cantrip.

It cannot change size/volume by more than 50% up or down. The base duration is 1 turn: a radical change lasts less (dead to living, for instance, lasts only 1 round), while a very slight change such as color lasts 1 or more days. Small, normal, non-magical creatures of animal intelligence get no saving throw. Components: typically a magic word while passing a hand over the object.

Everyone watching looks where the caster chooses, to his or her right or left and within 10 feet: at the caster’s right hand and a spot a few feet away where the finger points, say, while the left hand does something unnoticed. It lasts only 1 segment. Only individuals above 0 level, or with at least 1 + 1 hit dice and better than low intelligence, get a saving throw. Components: an attention-getting word or phrase and a gesture to the left or right.

Makes an object of almost any size invisible, for a short time, to everyone in front of the caster. It does not work on viewers beside or behind the caster, and it does not hide sound: a hidden crowing rooster can still be heard, and so can a hidden elephant’s tread, trumpeting or even breathing.

Duration: 1 turn for an object of 2 cubic yards or less, less 1 round for every 2 more cubic yards, down to 1 round at 20 cubic yards. Above 20 cubic yards, it loses 1 segment per 2 more cubic yards: 9 segments at 22 cubic yards, 8 at 24, 7 at 26, 6 at 28, 5 at 30, 4 at 32, 3 at 34, 2 at 36 and 1 segment at 38. Anything larger than 38 cubic yards will at best vanish for a moment and reappear.

Components: an activating word such as abracadabra while passing a hand across the front of the object. Speaking the word again ends the cantrip.

Changes the shape of small mineral objects of glass, metal, stone, etc.: a flat piece to a rod, a ring shape to a sphere, a coin to a ring. It can also change glass to crystal, lead to silver, copper to gold, etc. Magic items are too strong for it. It lasts only 1 round. If someone else touches the object, he or she makes a saving throw versus spell, and on a success the cantrip is dispelled. Components: similar to change.

Lets the caster secretly palm a small object. The cantrip makes an illusory copy of the object, while the real one is hidden by a form of hide (which works whatever the viewers’ position). The copy lasts only 1 segment, so it must be covered or screened, or onlookers will see it wink out. The caster speaks a special word while pointing at the object, and can then pick up the now-invisible real object while seeming only to touch or handle the copy.

Brings any small object or objects within 2 feet of the caster to his or her hand. They appear in the hand as the caster raises or holds it out with a flourish and speaks the key word. Something as large as a tankard uses up the cantrip, but up to a dozen coins could be brought before it fails. The caster must know exactly what and where the objects are. If they are on another person and not in plain sight, that person gets a saving throw versus spell.

The target belches involuntarily. The saving throw only decides how loud: on a failure, very loud; on a success, fairly low and muffled. Components: an almost silent belch while the caster presses his or her diaphragm.

The target blinks his, her or its eye or eyes for a moment, no more than half a second. On a successful saving throw it is just a single wink (or no effect for one-eyed creatures). Components: a softly spoken magic word (such as hat-cha-cha) while snapping the fingers.

The target coughs in spasms. On a successful saving throw it is only a brief hack that usually does not disturb other activities. On a failure it is a loud, active series of coughs lasting 1 to 3 seconds. Components: a gagging gesture and a gasp.

The target giggles involuntarily. On a failed saving throw it is a chuckle or giggle lasting about 2 or 3 seconds; on a success, only a brief chuckle. Components: a single word or phrase (known in magical circles as a “punch line”) while one finger moves rapidly back and forth.

A muscle contraction makes the target nod involuntarily, as if agreeing or greeting someone. A successful saving throw negates it. Components: a slight nod while pointing the little finger at the target.

The target feels an annoying itch somewhere and, unless it saves, scratches it involuntarily. The scratch takes a second and ends the itch at once. Components: naming some body pest (flea, louse, etc.) while pointing to where the itch is to be.
Irritates the target’s nose. Unless it saves versus spell, it sneezes once, which ends the irritation. Components: naming an irritant while touching one’s own nose.

A muscle in some part of the target (head, neck, hand, arm, foot, leg, etc.) twitches noticeably, but without real discomfort or loss of control or concentration. A successful saving throw negates it. Components: naming the body part while gazing at it and making a twitching hand motion.

The target winks one eye. On a successful saving throw the wink is quick and hardly noticeable; on a failure it is a greatly exaggerated, prolonged wink. Components: a magic phrase (such as twenty-three skidoo) while the caster winks almost imperceptibly.

The target feels a brief wave of drowsiness and yawns. A successful saving throw versus spell means no effect at all. On a failure, the target yawns at once and becomes more vulnerable to sleep for the rest of that round and all of the next:

  • It automatically falls into a comatose slumber if a sleep spell is cast on it, so where more than 1 creature of 4 or fewer hit dice is targeted by sleep, 1 extra creature is affected.
  • Among creatures of 4 + 1 to 4 + 4 hit dice, there is a chance that two are affected by sleep.
  • Even a creature of up to 5 + 2 hit dice can be put to sleep, rolled as if it had 4 + 1 to 4 + 4 hit dice (that is, a 50% chance it is not affected).

Components: humming a lullaby while making a rocking motion with cupped hands.

Summons a honey bee from somewhere (where does not matter) within seconds. It appears wherever the caster is looking, up to 1˝ away. It is annoyed, and 90% likely to sting any living creature it lands on (which will certainly make the target react violently if a bee sting would otherwise do so). Components: a low buzzing while moving a forefinger in flight-like passes.

Conjures a small, 3-inch sphere of glowing blue light. It looks eerie from a distance, but only lights an area 5’ around itself, and casts no reflections beyond that. It does not affect infravision or ultravision. When the caster says a rhyme using the words blue and light in any combination, it appears in his or her open palm and glows until the caster stops concentrating on it.

A variation of bee: summons a crawling insect (a beetle or bug) in the same way, at the spot pointed to up to 1˝ away. It is also irritated, and pinches, bites or otherwise attacks the creature it lands on, with appropriate results. Components: naming the insect wanted while the forefinger makes a sliding and pointing motion at the spot.

A jet of very hot flame up to one-half foot long shoots from the caster’s finger for up to 1 segment, easily lighting fairly dry combustibles such as parchment, twigs, kindling and the like. Components: a word of power over elemental fire (such as ron-son, zip-po, or the much revered dun-hill), with forefinger extended and a sideways flick of the thumb.

Like bee and bug, but summons a cloud of gnats, which at once fly around the head of the nearest living creature (no more than 1˝ from the caster). Unless it saves versus poison, the creature is distracted for 1-4 segments before the gnats fly off. Components: a high-pitched buzzing made with tongue and palate while pointing at where the cloud is to appear.

Like the bee and bug cantrips, but brings a mouse up to 1˝ from the caster: a typical field mouse, or as close a species as possible. The caster has no control over it, and it behaves as any mouse would in the situation. Components: a summoning word (usually the name of a food mice like) while holding the hands to look like mouse ears.

A puff of real smoke appears where the caster wishes, up to 1˝ away, and rises or disperses like normal smoke depending on conditions. It can be white, gray, black, brown, yellow or green. Components: naming the color while moving a hand from horizontal to vertical and breathing out a puff of air.

Like bee, bug, mouse or gnats, but summons a small ordinary spider to a spot up to 1˝ from the caster: usually a common garden spider or the like, no more than an inch or two across, and basically harmless. There is a 5% chance it is one with powerful poison (black widow, brown recluse, etc.). Annoyed, it immediately bites any creature it lands on.

  • Normal spider: only a momentary effect, distracting the victim for 1 segment.
  • Very poisonous spider: the victim also saves versus poison at +4. On a success, 1 point of damage. On a failure, 2 points of damage, and the victim feels sick and cannot act normally for 1-4 days unless neutralize poison removes the toxin (slow poison delays the sickness for 1 day).

Components: saying the word arachnid while spreading and wiggling the fingers.

An unseen thumb and forefinger harmlessly but annoyingly tweak a chosen target within 1˝ of the caster, on the cheek, nose, ear, beard, moustache, whiskers or tail. It does not disturb spell casting, but may distract a creature as it turns to find the source. A creature with intelligence under 7 that fails a saving throw versus spell, or one with intelligence 7 or more that fails to roll above its intelligence on 3d6, is distracted for 1 segment.
