People passing through seem to leave tracks, tear cobwebs, and so on. Unless they actually touch something the spell hides, the place seems empty of its real contents. It is a very powerful mix of advanced invisibility and illusion, but it can only hide non-living things; living things are not hidden, though their presence does not disturb the spell.

Merely brushing a hidden object does not disturb it; only forceful contact gives any chance of noticing that things are not as they seem. Even then, a creature sees through it only if it finds several items it cannot “see”, and then gets a saving throw versus spell; failure means it believes only those objects are invisible.

Dispel illusion or dispel magic removes it, showing the area as it really is. True seeing, a gem of seeing and similar effects see through it, but detect invisibility does not.

Component: a square of the finest black silk worth at least 100 gp.

Essentially a spectral forces spell run by a program set by the caster (much like programmed illusion), so the illusionist need only concentrate for 5 segments after casting, after which the program carries on by itself. The illusion has sight, full sound, smell and heat. A viewer who actively tries to disbelieve gets a saving throw versus spell. If one succeeds and tells other viewers who can understand, each of them gets a saving throw at +4.

Components: a bit of fleece and several grains of sand.

A much more limited form of limited wish. The illusionist must find a comfortable place, lie down, concentrate on the desired result, and sleep. After at least 8 hours of undisturbed sleep, the dream takes effect 1 to 12 hours later. Typical results:

  • Recovering a person’s lost hit points
  • Restoring a body part such as a hand or foot
  • Finding some object not heavily guarded by magic wards and protections
  • Discovering a way in or out
  • Finding a safe path through a wilderness
  • Improving the chance of gaining a rich treasure
  • Learning the approximate strength of enemy forces. A creature scried this way that has 7+ or more hit dice may save versus spell; if it succeeds, the dream does not detect it, and it may even sense the illusionist as if detecting invisible.

This list is the maximum a dream can do, and its results never permanently go beyond these limits. If a companion recently slain in battle were dreamed alive, for example, he or she would live for only 1 turn per level of the illusionist, then return to his or her previous state; more permanent magic would be needed to bring the companion back fully.

Extension and permanency cannot affect a dream. It can be used only once per week; a second casting in the same week absolutely fails, and the illusionist ages 1-10 years.

rolls.label: Aging if cast twice in a week (years)

system.description: Virtually the same as the 4th-level magic-user spell of the same name, with the same material components, except that if the illusionist casts a vision spell in place of the normal material components, the mirror scries properly (though the vision spell itself does not work normally).

A powerful illusion that affects the minds and bodies of everyone in the area, including anyone who enters later, so that time seems to pass much faster: every turn (10 minutes) feels like a full hour. All their bodily functions speed up to match, so they must eat, sleep and so forth at the faster rate, and other spells cast in the area run their durations faster too. One hour is like six to them, and four hours like a full day. This lets them rest, regain spells and recover lost hit points.

Reverse: the caster can instead slow time for those affected: an hour seems only a turn, a day only four hours. No special preparation is needed.

The illusionist is affected either way. With the reverse, the effect always lasts at least one turn after the caster wants it to end, because his or her reactions are so greatly slowed.

Creates an area of solid fog that is also highly acidic and deadly to living things. Plants die in it: grass and similar small plants in 2 rounds, bushes and shrubs in 4, small trees in 8, large trees in 16 rounds. Animal life not immune to acid takes damage depending on how long it is exposed:

  • 1st round: 1 point
  • 2nd round: 2 points
  • 3rd round: 4 points
  • 4th & each later round: 8 points

Otherwise it is the same as solid fog. Components: a pinch of dried, powdered peas, powdered animal hoof, and strong acid of any kind (including highly distilled vinegar or acid crystals).

Creates a phantasmal double of the illusionist while cloaking the real illusionist in improved invisibility. The illusionist can then go elsewhere while the double seems to walk away. The double can speak and gesture as if real, with full smell and touch as well. Detect illusion, true seeing, true sight or a gem of seeing reveals the double as an illusion; detect invisibility, true sight, true seeing, a gem of seeing or a robe of eyes can detect the invisible illusionist (cf. shadow door).

system.aoe: 4 square ˝ + 1 square ˝ per level of caster
system.description: Prepares a special spectral forces illusion that is triggered by a particular action. It usually includes full sight, sound, smell and touch, and always involves falling, sliding or rushing movement (or a dwindling perspective), either of the subjects themselves or of something else; this is what sets it apart from programmed illusion. For example, it might trigger on falling into a pit, reaching the center of an area, opening a door, or a similar act, and the subjects then believe the fall goes on for scores of feet, that a pit has opened and they are sliding helplessly into the unknown, that a wall of water is rushing at them from beyond the door, or whatever.

Like vacancy, but more powerful and elaborate; also similar to the mirage cantrip. The caster makes an area look like whatever he or she imagines, but always some place he or she has actually seen. It lasts while the caster keeps faint concentration on it (possible during normal conversation, but not while casting spells, in melee, or after being hurt by an attack), and for 6 turns plus 1 turn per level after that.

Two forms:

  • Basic (3 segments to cast): short of a detection device or spell, only forceful contact and touch give any hope of discovering it.
  • Complex (6 segments, with a material component, a small bit of anything connected with the place shown): it takes on a form of reality, and only magical means (device, item or spell) can detect it.

Either form can be removed by dispel illusion or dispel magic.

Effects of belief: as with all powerful illusions, the viewer’s mind affects his or her body, though belief cannot usually change the laws of nature and magic. A viewer might walk across hot coals thinking them a cool shallow stream (and take no damage), dine on imaginary food and actually be nourished, or rest comfortably on sharp stones thinking them a featherbed. But gravity is not affected: an imagined bridge over a deep chasm will not hold the believer up. Onlookers just see the person suddenly vanish, and will not connect it with an illusion unless they already know magic is at work.

The illusionist must be in an area of heavy shadow. The caster, and any creatures he or she touches, are carried to the edge of the Prime Material Plane where it borders the Plane of Shadow. There the illusionist can move at a relative rate of up to 7 leagues per turn, moving normally along the borders of the Plane of Shadow while aware of where he or she is relative to the Prime Material Plane. Stepping back onto the Prime Material Plane at the chosen destination allows very fast travel. It can also be used to reach other planes bordering the Plane of Shadow, but that needs a rather dangerous crossing of the Plane of Shadow to reach another border.

Creatures taken along can follow the illusionist, wander off into Shadowland, or stumble back onto the Prime Material Plane (50% chance of either if the illusionist loses or abandons them). Unwilling creatures get a saving throw that negates the effect.

The illusionist must be able to talk with the target(s), calling out during the casting that their final fate, their doom, is upon them. Even those who make their saving throw are paralyzed by fear for a full 7 segments and lose 1-4 points of strength, which return after 7 rounds.

Those who fail to save versus spell must face their nemesis, the opponent(s) they most fear and hate. They must fight it, since no magical escape is possible, and the foe is real for all intents and purposes. If they lose, they die. If they kill the weird, they emerge with no damage, no loss of items they seemed to use in the fight, and no loss of spells they seemed to cast, and gain experience for defeating it if applicable. Each round of combat seems normal but takes only 1 segment of real time. The illusionist must concentrate fully on the spell throughout.
